title: 1967 AHSME Problem 15
statement: The difference in the areas of two similar triangles is \(18\) square feet, and the ratio of the larger area to the smaller is the square of an integer. The area of the smaller triangle, in square feet, is an integer, and one of its sides is \(3\) feet. The corresponding side of the larger triangle, in feet, is:

solutions.text:
Let the side-scale factor be the integer \(k\gt1\) and the smaller area be the integer \(T.\) Then \[ T(k^2-1)=18. \] Thus \(k^2-1\) is a positive divisor of \(18.\) The only resulting square \(k^2\) is \(4,\) so \(k=2.\) The corresponding side is \(3k=6.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is D.
hints: Let the integer side-scale factor be \(k\)
If the smaller area is \(T,\) then \(T(k^2-1)=18\)
